name: JW Marriott Jeju Resort & Spa
positioning: Clifftop resort in Seogwipo on Jeju Island, the first JW Marriott Resort and Spa in South Korea, with interiors by Bill Bensley, ocean-view rooms and a heated infinity pool
best_for: Travelers who want ocean views from a clifftop island resort
Design lovers drawn to Bill Bensley interiors inspired by Jeju's landscape
Families wanting family suites with bunk beds and a kids club

facts.text: The resort has a clifftop setting in Seogwipo City on Jeju Island.
It was the first JW Marriott Resort and Spa in South Korea.
Bill Bensley designed the interiors, drawing inspiration from Jeju's canola fields and basalt walls.
Bensley chose yellow as the main color for its symbolic representation of luck in Korean culture, with gray, black and white echoing Jeju's volcanic terrain.
Architecture firm WATG drew inspiration from Korea's indigenous Choga architecture and Jeju's terrain.
Most rooms include a balcony with ocean views.
SPA by JW offers Hot Stone, Deep Tissue and Swedish treatments in five treatment rooms.
The resort has a jimjilbang, a Korean-style sauna with various themed rooms.
The resort's RE CONNECT activity program is curated for families, couples, solo guests and children.
The Flying Hog is a wood-fire grill showcasing Jeju's seasonal ingredients.
Yeoumul offers a chef-led journey inspired by Jeju's haenyeo culture.

highlights.text: The JW Garden sits alongside the Jeju Olle Trail route 7, with views of the sea.
The outdoor pool is a heated infinity pool with a swim-up bar.
The Panorama Suite is designed to offer ocean views from every angle.
Soombi-Sori is a meditation and breathing experience inspired by Jeju's haenyeo, the island's female divers.
The Family Suite has a king bedroom, a second bedroom with two twin bunk beds for children, and a separate living room.

considerations.text: Jeju International Airport is about 40 km from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing for the luxury resort experience.
